---
title: "Comparison with typically developing children"
abstract: "*How vocabulary growth in children with Down syndrome compares with typically developing children. We present two complementary views: trajectories aligned by chronological age, which show the developmental time lag; and relationships aligned by words understood, which ask whether the structure of word learning — in particular how production tracks comprehension — differs beyond that lag. Down syndrome estimates come from the models of record (VG10; VG01/VG02); typically developing estimates from the TD reference models (VG11/VG12/VG13).*"

## Aligned by words understood {#sec-comparison-vocab}

The question of primary interest: setting age aside, does production track comprehension *the same way* in the two groups — or is there a **structural difference beyond the time lag**?

**TODO**: plot the production ratio $q$ (@sec-ratios) and words spoken **as a function of words understood** (not age) for DS (VG10) and TD (VG13/VG06) on common axes.

- If the curves **overlay**, the difference between groups is consistent with a developmental time lag: at a given vocabulary size, children produce the same fraction of what they understand.
- If they **diverge**, there is a structural difference in the comprehension→production mapping itself — e.g. a wider or narrower understood-to-spoken gap in Down syndrome at matched comprehension levels.
